headline: U.S.–Iran Fire Resumes as Oil Prices Jump
seoTitle: U.S.–Iran Fire Resumes, Oil Prices Rise | FMB Worldwide
seoDescription: The U.S. and Iran exchanged attacks again after a month-long lull, pushing oil prices higher and renewing concern over the Strait of Hormuz.
deck: Renewed strikes around the Strait of Hormuz have put energy markets and regional security back on alert.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The United States and Iran exchanged attacks over the weekend for the first time in about a month. U.S. forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz, while Iran said it retaliated against U.S. sites in Jordan.
The United Arab Emirates said Monday that it intercepted an Iranian drone over its territorial waters. Oil prices rose more than 2% as markets reacted to the renewed escalation.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most important oil-shipping routes. Any sustained disruption can quickly affect crude prices, transport costs and inflation expectations well beyond the Middle East.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: For the Philippines, higher global oil prices can feed into fuel, transport and electricity costs. The immediate risk is not only military escalation but also prolonged pressure on energy prices and shipping confidence.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for further U.S. or Iranian strikes, changes in commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, new sanctions, and whether diplomatic contacts produce a pause in hostilities.
